Circular action

.dr-btn--icon · --danger-solid · --night · --night[aria-pressed] · --onphoto · --primary.dr-btn--icon · components/button.css · components/media.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

  1. 1.dr-btn--iconThe disc: 44 × 44, border-radius:50%, no border and no shadow. HIG · 44pt exactly, 1.83× WCAG 2.5.8's 24 × 24. z-index:2, so it clears a whole-card link.
  2. 2.dr-icThe 20px glyph, rendered stroke 1.42. It is the only content, so the accessible name lives in aria-label, and it is the glyph, not the disc, that carries WCAG 1.4.11.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Circular icon action; Icon action on a photograph; End call; Call control; Send action.

When to use

A circular action is an icon-only command: one glyph whose meaning is unambiguous where it stands, so the label can be dropped. It is the shape of every icon-only button in the product, one 44 disc on different grounds for different jobs. The default stands on light surfaces: Delete order, View details and View the photo and video set on order-history, Download video on order-details-aerial, and Swap pickup and drop-off in the route card of listings, listings-filters, listings-loading and listings-error. --night and --danger-solid stand on the call surface (call, call-aerial, call-inspection, call-client, call-support). --onphoto stands on the video cover of order-details-aerial, and the green Send in the composer of chat, chat-aerial, chat-inspection and chat-client.

The words are the accessible name, so they carry the whole meaning: a verb and its object, End call, Send message, Play video · 0:38. Not Hang up, not End alone. A toggle keeps one name and states its condition in aria-pressed.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Circular icon action · § Destructive fill · § Call control · § Circular action as a screen's primary · inventory.md § 1 (Circular icon action, Icon action on a photograph, End call, Call control, Send action) · microcopy.md § call, chat

Rule and anti-rule

Do

Icon-only where the glyph is the convention, each with an aria-label that names verb and object. The red fill goes only to the one destructive control, End call.

Don’t

A disc with no aria-label has no accessible name (WCAG 4.1.2), and the red fill spent on a command that is not ending a call. When the action needs words to be understood, such as cancelling an order or paying, use a labelled button. To offer a set of routes, use a sheet.
